title: Learn to Recognize the Road
headline: Am I Growing If I Still Struggle?
tagline: You may not recognize the destination yet, but you can learn to recognize the road.
seo_title: Am I Growing If I Still Struggle? Hebrews 12:1-2 for Men | TheWrkShop
seo_description: Growth doesn't always mean the battle disappears; sometimes it changes how you fight it. A devotional for men on direction, return and Hebrews 12:1-2.
verse_text: ….let us run with perseverance the race marked out for us, fixing our eyes on Jesus.…

scriptures.text: ….let us run with perseverance the race marked out for us, fixing our eyes on Jesus.…
Give careful thought to the paths for your feet and be steadfast in all your ways.

items: We tend to evaluate spiritual growth by destination.
But Scripture frequently uses another category:
Maybe you still struggle with anger.
You used to rehearse the offense for three weeks.
Now you recognize what is happening after thirty minutes.
You used to hide for days after failure. Now you confess.
You used to spiral before remembering Scripture. Now truth enters sooner.
You used to defend yourself immediately. Now there is a pause.

sections.label: Maturity May Look Like a Quicker Return

items: Grace is what makes return possible.
But increasing responsiveness can be evidence of formation.

blocks.text: “If I struggle again, I must not be growing.”

items: That lie turns one difficult moment into discouragement.
Then “This is just who I am.”
Growth does not always mean the disappearance of battle. Sometimes growth changes how you fight it.
Comparison measures position. Discipleship pays attention to direction and allegiance.
Don’t turn wandering into residence. Return.
